title: Strings in Depth
summary: Indexing, slicing, and the string methods you'll reach for constantly.

checkpoints.title: Indexing and slicing
checkpoints.content: A string is a sequence of characters, counted from 0. `name = "Python"` then `name[0]` is `"P"`. Slicing with `name[1:4]` gives characters at positions 1, 2, and 3 (the end index is never included) — `"yth"`.
checkpoints.explanation: Slicing's end index being exclusive trips almost everyone up at first — `name[1:4]` gets 3 characters (4 - 1), not 4.

hints.H1: `name[a:b]` includes index a but stops right before index b.

checkpoints.title: Slice a string
checkpoints.content: Given `word = "hello"`, write an expression that returns just `"ell"`.
checkpoints.explanation: "ell" is the characters at indexes 1, 2, and 3 — so the slice runs from 1 up to (but not including) 4.

hints.H1: You need 3 characters, starting from index 1.

checkpoints.title: Predict a string method

options.explanation: .strip() removes the leading/trailing spaces, then .lower() lowercases the result.
.strip() removes the surrounding whitespace before .lower() even runs — the spaces don't survive.
.lower() lowercases every letter, including the capital H — it doesn't preserve casing.

checkpoints.explanation: String methods chain left to right: .strip() runs first (removing the surrounding spaces), then .lower() runs on that result.

hints.H0: Methods chained with dots run in order, left to right.
hints.H1: .strip() only removes whitespace from the ends, not the middle.
hints.H2: The result is "hello" — no spaces, all lowercase.

checkpoints.title: Build an f-string
checkpoints.content: Given `name = "Ada"` and `age = 30`, write an f-string that produces exactly: `Ada is 30 years old`
checkpoints.explanation: An f-string embeds variables directly inside `{}` placeholders, without manual string concatenation.

hints.H0: f-strings start with an `f` right before the opening quote.
hints.H1: Put each variable name inside its own pair of curly braces.
